transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58m
Attendees: Carlos Mendes (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Maya Lin (ApolloRx - Head of MLOps), Rajat Singh (ApolloRx - SRE), Keisha Brown (ApolloRx - Security), Tom Alvarez (ApolloRx - PM)

Auto-generated summary (may contain errors): demo of Redwood console for tracing and root cause discovery. Focus on request correlation and KV cache fallbacks. Discussed compliance and VPC options.

[00:00] Carlos Mendes: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we can start in about a minute but welcome from Redwood, I'm Carlos, AE, with Priya and Liam from the SE team. how's everyone doing?
[00:28] Maya Lin: good, thanks. we're excited to see how your console stitches traces for our multi-model pipeline. we have some nasty fallback cases that we want visibility into.
[01:05] Priya Shah: awesome, that's exactly what we'll show — how traces correlate across the request graph, where KV cache misses happen, and how the runtime falls back to a heavier model variant. quick note: some of our auto-transcripts call KV "kay-vee" or "K-V" so sorry if it looks weird.
[01:40] Rajat Singh: perfect. our primary concern is latency SLOs — we can't have p95 spikes over 800ms for inference paths that are synchronous to user flows. also data retention and PHI leakage — we need auditability.
[02:15] Carlos Mendes: totally, Keisha and Tom — you mentioned security requirements in the pre-call. can you restate the must-haves?
[02:33] Keisha Brown: sure. SOC2 is baseline. we need KMS for key management (customer-managed preferred), VPC peering or private deployment, and retention of request metadata for 90 days. also RBAC and SSO via SAML.
[02:52] Carlos Mendes: good — all of that is supported; we'll point to the whitepaper after.
[03:10] Priya Shah: OK jumping into the console — I'm going to share my screen. first, the request index view shows each request with a request id, model variant, route, and latency columns. you can filter by model, user id, or correlation id.
[03:40] [screen share noise / slight echo]
[04:05] Priya Shah: here's an example request that triggered a fallback. note the trace tree on the right — top node is API gateway, then routing, model inference node, KV cache lookup, fallback path. you can expand nodes to see logs and the raw request/response payloads.
[04:35] Tom Alvarez: quick Q — is the payload itself stored in the console or only pointers? for PHI we prefer not to persist full user text.
[04:50] Liam O'Connor: good question. by default we store request metadata and a redacted payload; full payload capture is opt-in and customers can configure retention or disable. in private deployment you control storage and can plug into your KMS/HSM.
[05:22] Maya Lin: ok that helps. show us how you correlate multiple model hits for the same user request — e.g., candidate generation then reranker then final prompt.
[05:40] Priya Shah: yeah, so our tracing adds a correlation_id at the platform layer — you can search that id and see the entire request journey across models. in the trace view we'll highlight latency hotspots — nodes with high duration are orange/red. here's a synthetic example where the reranker added 220ms because it switched to a "full precision" variant.
[06:15] Rajat Singh: are those variant names consistent with our catalog? we don't want opaque names like v1-abc.
[06:28] Priya Shah: they match the model catalog tags; you can map tags to friendly names in the settings. sometimes the auto-transcript munges names though — e.g., 'redwood-optimize' gets written as 'redwood optima' — apologies for that.
[06:55] [brief crosstalk]
[07:20] Priya Shah: next, error mapping — each error is attached to the node where it happened and we capture stack-ish traces for the runtime side. you can see error frequency over time and correlate to deployment rollouts.
[07:45] Maya Lin: show a real example from production?
[08:00] Liam O'Connor: yeah, here's a real trace from a customer where a KV cache eviction caused downstream reroutes. trace shows cache miss at time T, fallback to CPU host, queueing delay, and then p95 spike. the console links the request id to the exact model config and the node's logs.
[08:35] Keisha Brown: can we export these logs to our SIEM? we want them in Splunk for audits.
[08:50] Carlos Mendes: yes, export to S3 or push to your SIEM via our log forwarder; in private deployments you can retain logs in your own storage. we'll share the export spec.
[09:15] Priya Shah: another useful view is the request timeline — it stitches request events like client receive, routing, KV read, model decode, and send. each event has a timestamp and duration. you can jump from an event to the underlying logs.
[09:45] Tom Alvarez: how do you surface intermittent tokenization errors? sometimes tokenizers behave differently across quantized and full-precision paths.
[10:02] Priya Shah: we log tokenizer warnings and compare token counts across variants; if counts differ we flag a tokenization mismatch and show sample inputs.
[10:30] Rajat Singh: the part I worry about is consistent reproducibility — if we replay a trace do we get identical behavior?
[10:45] Liam O'Connor: replay is deterministic to the degree the model and environment match. for bench runs we recommend pinning model versions and using the same quantization profile; our replay tool will surface any environment mismatch.
[11:10] [pause]
[11:25] Priya Shah: ok moving on, here's the fallback dashboard — it aggregates failures by type (KV miss, OOM, timeout, model error). you can set alerts for thresholds, e.g., >1% fallback rate triggers a page.
[11:50] Maya Lin: what's the instrumentation overhead for tracing? we can't add too much latency.
[12:05] Priya Shah: instrumentation is lightweight; most metadata is added at the serving layer and doesn't change token payload. overhead is typically sub-millisecond per request for the trace header, and cost is dominated by model inference.
[12:32] Keisha Brown: for audit logs, we need immutable records of which model versions served what in case of later compliance reviews. how long do you keep these by default?
[12:45] Carlos Mendes: hosted default is 30 days, but we offer extended retention as an add-on. in Dedicated or Private you can set retention policies — we'll provide the retention APIs in the docs.
[13:05] Tom Alvarez: I'd like to see a demo of a KV miss causing a fallback — the end-to-end view including how the console surfaces the decision.
[13:20] Priya Shah: sure — Liam will run a live replay. Liam, do you want to kick it off?
[13:27] Liam O'Connor: yep I'll trigger a replay of a synthetic trace where the KV returns null for 1 out of 10 requests. starting now...
[13:40] [background hum as Liam runs job]
[14:05] Liam O'Connor: replay done — you can see the request tree where the KV node reports miss count 1, fallback to larger model, and the downstream latency increase. the console also shows if the fallback used a different quantization profile.
[14:40] Rajat Singh: can we simulate higher load? our traffic pattern is highly spiky — bursts to 500 qps for 30s.
[14:55] Liam O'Connor: yes our load runner can replay bursts; for the pilot we'll run your trace at scaled qps to measure p95 and fallback rate.
[15:20] Maya Lin: for the pilot, we'd like to know what configuration to supply — model samples, a representative traffic log, and expected SLOs.
[15:33] Carlos Mendes: that's in the benchmark template Priya will share.
[15:45] Priya Shah: linked in chat: https://redwood-demo.internal/pilot-template (shared). the template asks for a 24-48 hour traffic dump, model artifacts, and the keys for any private repos (we can run via secure transfer).
[16:10] Keisha Brown: about private deploys — can the control plane be customer-hosted? we prefer the control plane in our VPC for regulated workloads.
[16:25] Carlos Mendes: yes, we have a Private option where control plane sits in your account. we also support a hybrid: control plane hosted but logs and model artifacts in your VPC. KMS integration is supported; we can document exact HSM/KMS supported versions.
[16:50] Rajat Singh: network egress — do you need open outbound to internet? we need to restrict to internal endpoints only.
[17:05] Liam O'Connor: for Private deployment, no internet egress required; we can peer straight to your subnets and use internal registries.
[17:20] [brief silence]
[17:35] Priya Shah: ok back to the console — here's the root cause drilldown flow: pick a time window, filter by route or model, identify high-latency traces, then root cause using the event timeline and node logs. you can tag traces and add internal notes.
[18:00] Tom Alvarez: is tagging integrated with our ticketing system? e.g., create a JIRA with trace link.
[18:12] Priya Shah: yes we have integrations for JIRA and PagerDuty; you can attach trace context to tickets.
[18:30] Maya Lin: do you provide programmatic access to traces? we want to run offline analysis.
[18:40] Liam O'Connor: yes trace export API — JSONL stream of events, with correlation ids and timestamps. we'll share the schema.
[19:05] Keisha Brown: are there PII redaction tools? we don't want raw PII in logs.
[19:18] Priya Shah: we support automatic redaction patterns and allow custom regex masks. in private deployments, redaction can run in your environment before logs leave.
[19:40] Rajat Singh: earlier you mentioned token-level cost breakdowns — can we get per-request cost estimates?
[19:55] Carlos Mendes: yes, the cost panel shows tokens consumed per stage and an estimated cost per request. you can export that to align with billing.
[20:20] [30 second narration of UI by Priya]
[20:55] Priya Shah: ok switching to alerting — you can set SLOs per route, for p95/p99, and configure automatic rollbacks or model variant fallbacks if SLOs degrade. here is a sample canary policy we use.
[21:30] Tom Alvarez: rollback automation worries me — we need a manual approval gate.
[21:40] Priya Shah: absolutely, policies can include manual gates and Slack approvals; you can also configure silent canaries that only alert but don't modify routing.
[21:55] Maya Lin: show us how the console surfaces anomalies over time — we want to detect regressions after deployments.
[22:10] Liam O'Connor: here's the quality monitoring dashboard — it ties eval prompts to production traces so you can see drift. if a prompt set shows a quality regression, you can correlate to a rollout and immediately identify which model change caused it.
[22:45] Keisha Brown: for compliance, we need an immutable audit trail of who approved rollouts.
[22:55] Carlos Mendes: we capture approvals and audit events with user ids and timestamps; these are available via API and audit logs.
[23:20] [customer side chat about internal stakeholder timing]
[23:50] Tom Alvarez: timeline question — we want to run a 2-week pilot and then decide by end of May. is that feasible?
[24:05] Carlos Mendes: yes, 2-week pilot is typical. we'll scope the pilot with Priya and Liam and provide success criteria.
[24:30] Priya Shah: ok I'm going to demo a small SLO alert flow — creating an alert for fallback rate > 0.5% over 5m. creating now... saved. note you can route alerts to Slack or PagerDuty.
[25:05] Rajat Singh: can alerts be rate-limited? we don't want noisy pages.
[25:18] Priya Shah: yes, suppression windows and dedupe rules are supported.
[25:35] [10m montage of interactive UI exploration, timestamps advancing]
[35:50] Priya Shah: one last demo — correlation across multi-tenant traffic. if you have multiple product lines we can tag traffic and produce per-tenant dashboards with RBAC.
[36:10] Maya Lin: that's important. we run multiple models for different brands and need tenant-level SLOs.
[36:30] Carlos Mendes: we can do that with route-level tagging and schema enforcement.
[36:48] Keisha Brown: security question — do you rotate keys automatically or do we manage rotation in our KMS?
[36:58] Liam O'Connor: rotation is customer-managed for Private; for hosted we offer rotation options and can integrate with customer KMS for automatic rotation.
[37:20] Tom Alvarez: any gotchas for running quantized models with tracing? we've seen mismatches across hardware.
[37:35] Priya Shah: hardware variations matter; console will surface if quantization profile differs between hosts. for production we recommend pinning the quantization and testing with a small rollout.
[38:05] Rajat Singh: ok can you show the import/export flow for model artifacts? we use private registries.
[38:20] Liam O'Connor: model import supports OCI-compatible registries and S3 buckets; for private deployments we'll show how to configure internal registries.
[38:45] [short pause]
[39:00] Priya Shah: wrapping up demo section — we've covered trace correlation, fallback dashboards, alerting, replay, and integrations.
[39:15] Maya Lin: this was helpful. couple follow-ups: 1) send SOC2 + KMS docs, 2) pilot template, 3) sample replay results for KV fallback.
[39:30] Carlos Mendes: we'll send those. Priya — Liam — anything to add?
[39:40] Liam O'Connor: I'll include a CSV of synthetic replay results and notes on configuration tweaks.
[39:50] Priya Shah: I'll include the pilot checklist and trace schema.
[40:05] Tom Alvarez: switching to pricing quick check — what are the cost levers we should be aware of during pilot?
[40:18] Carlos Mendes: main levers are model size/variant, quantization, batching, and KV hit rate. Redwood Optimize recommendations can suggest batching thresholds to reduce token cost without breaking latency.
[40:35] Maya Lin: will Optimize run on our traces?
[40:42] Priya Shah: yes, Optimize can analyze your trace corpus and propose configurations; we'll include a sample Optimize report.
[40:55] Keisha Brown: final compliance check: can we get a statement of data flow for our legal team? they need mapping of where any PHI could go.
[41:10] Carlos Mendes: yes we'll generate a data flow diagram for the pilot and the private deployment option.
[41:30] [short break in audio]
[41:50] Maya Lin: ok let's confirm next steps and owners.
[42:00] Carlos Mendes: action items in chat: Priya to share pilot template; Carlos to share SOC2/KMS; Liam to run synthetic KV fallback and share results; schedule kickoff for next Thursday?
[42:20] Tom Alvarez: next Thursday works for us.
[42:35] Rajat Singh: one more technical note — we'd like to test replay with our pre-tokenized samples; can you accept tokenized inputs?
[42:48] Liam O'Connor: yeah we can accept token-level payloads for replays; we'll document the format.
[43:05] Keisha Brown: also include redaction settings in the pilot checklist.
[43:18] Priya Shah: will do.
[43:30] [closing statements]
[43:50] Carlos Mendes: thanks everyone — we'll send notes and links within 24 hours. any final questions?
[44:05] Maya Lin: none from me. thanks.
[44:20] Tom Alvarez: thanks all.
[44:35] Priya Shah: thank you — we'll follow up.
[57:40] [meeting end recorded]
